Benchmark source from a real-world stream

Source: R/dsg_benchmark.R
dsg_source_data.Rd

Turns a real-world data stream into a dsg_source() whose real and virtual drift are controlled (Hinder et al., 2026). The stream, assumed to be in time order, is split into blocks twice:

  • virtual_blocks time segments give the feature distributions, sampled with replacement from the rows of each segment (virtual drift);

  • real_blocks time segments are given to a model of \(P(y \mid \tilde{T}, x)\), where \(\tilde{T}\) is the segment index; the labels of every concept are sampled from that model with the index of a segment fixed (real drift).

Labelling the data of any feature segment with the model of any label segment separates the virtual drift between segments from the real drift learned by the model, giving (virtual_blocks + 1) * (real_blocks + 1) concepts with known drift between them.

Usage

dsg_source_data(
  data,
  target,
  real_blocks = 5,
  virtual_blocks = 5,
  model = NULL,
  nodesize = 10,
  n_clusters = 0,
  n_ignore = 3,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

Data frame with the stream in time order. Every column but target must be numeric.

target

Name of the label column.

real_blocks, virtual_blocks

Number of segment boundaries (giving one more segment), or the boundaries themselves as relative positions in (0, 1) or as row indices.

model

Function model(x, y) that fits a classifier on the data frame x (with the segment index in column block) and returns a function giving a matrix of class probabilities (one column per class, named after the classes) for new data. NULL uses a random forest from the randomForest package (100 trees, nodesize as given).

nodesize

Minimum leaf size of the default random forest.

n_clusters

When greater than 0, the real drift is enhanced with region-wise label flips: the data are split into (n_ignore + 1) * real_blocks * n_clusters k-means clusters, and in each segment the labels of a segment-specific subset of the clusters are permuted among the classes.

n_ignore

Controls the share of clusters that are never flipped.

...

Further arguments for dsg_source(), such as test_size.

Value

dsg_source object (also of class dsg_source_data)

Details

With the default model, obj$quality holds the out-of-bag accuracy of the forest (how well the labelling model fits the data) and the permutation importance of the segment index (how much real drift the model found).

References

Hinder, F., Brinkrolf, J., Lammers, K., and Hammer, B. (2026). Real vs. Virtual Drift: Creating Realistic Stream Learning Benchmarks. In ESANN 2026, 133-138.

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
n <- 600
x1 <- c(stats::rnorm(300), stats::rnorm(300, 2))
x2 <- stats::rnorm(n)
y <- as.integer(x2 > c(rep(0, 300), rep(1, 300)))
stream <- data.frame(x1, x2, y)
source <- dsg_source_data(stream, "y", real_blocks = 1, virtual_blocks = 1,
                          test_size = 200, n_perm = 200)
dsg_stream(source, "-v-r", batch_size = 100)$segments
#>   segment type drift virtual_state real_state p_value label_change
#> 1       1    -     0             2          2      NA           NA
#> 2       2    v     1             1          2       0           NA
#> 3       3    -     0             1          2      NA           NA
#> 4       4    r     2             1          1      NA        0.305
# }
